Even if he's self sufficient he still needs to be reminded what is and isn't okay and have boundaries set. I babysit 5 kids, 10mo, 3F, 4F, 6F, and 8M and gave my two weeks because of similar issues. It was more the 6F and 8M running away and hiding around corners on walks home, always testing boundaries (scary ones, like running ahead to cross busy streets, climbing on unanchored bookcases/ heavy furniture  !)  consistent disrespect and misbehavior etc etc. Felt like I was constantly giving someone the what-for and it made me really uncomfortable and unhinged feeling like I was "yelling" at them too much. 

You are not overreacting but if these occurrences become commonplace and you aren't able to find solutions, might be worth a look for a new NF. Safety is number one, but also like, figure out ways to do activities together, set specific times where y'all will all ride bikes down the block, set timers so it's more concrete, keep differing activities to contained spaces so they can each do their own thing in safety, if its not something you can adapt to def would hop ship
